decision: The ticket was closed as completed on the strength of an untrusted provider email whose completion date ("November 4th", event-016) cannot belong to this job (reported 6 April 2026, instructed 13 April 2026), with no photos, no invoice, no tenant confirmation and the landlord-confirmation check still open (event-022). The same ticket also carries two different occupant identities (Isaac Quinn / 07700 900844 at event-009 and event-010 vs "Grace Ashford" / 07700 900641 at event-011), so it is not established which flat was attended — an authoritative-record conflict that changes the action (ESC-CONFLICT, RTE-STAFF). I did not re-open or re-dispatch (no duplicate work order) and did not decide liability or payment. In-authority reversible steps taken: tenant asked to confirm attendance and that the machine now drains (ACT-1); provider asked for the real attendance date, works done, photos and invoice (ACT-2); conflict recorded (ACT-3). A human must decide whether the closure stands.
recap: Closed washing-machine ticket rests on an unverifiable provider completion claim and conflicting tenant identities; verification sent, escalated to decide if closure stands.

next_step: Property manager to decide whether to reverse the closure, pending the tenant's confirmation that the machine drains and Oakfield Homes' attendance date/invoice (both requested today).
